itens.titulo: Nvidia, Oracle, CoreWeave and other AI stocks sink on OpenAI revenue report
itens.descricao: Nvidia, Oracle, CoreWeave and other AI stocks sink on OpenAI revenue report CNBC
trechos: OpenAI told investors that it hit roughly $50 billion in annualized revenue at the end of September, CNBC confirmed, lower than the the $68 billion figure that was widely reported late last month.
A person familiar with the matter said the $68 billion figure included gross revenue from OpenAI's partners, which helps investors make a more direct comparison with its chief rival, Anthropic.
The Financial Times was first to report the $50 billion figure.

In addition to the $50 billion in annualized revenue, OpenAI touted 77% total run rate growth during its third quarter, as well as 107% run rate growth for its enterprise business during the same period, the person said.
The company is under pressure to justify its $852 billion valuation to investors as it gears up for what is widely expected to be a blockbuster IPO.
OpenAI confidentially filed its prospectus with regulators in June, and executives have signaled that the company is eyeing a 2027 debut.
The company could raise around $30 billion, as CNBC previously reported, but that figure could change.
OpenAI closed a historic $122 billion funding round in March, and CFO Sarah Friar told CNBC last week that it is still "very well capitalized."

itens.titulo: Bitcoin price news: BTC falls to $80,000 nearly one year after October 2025 crash
itens.descricao: Bitcoin price news: BTC falls to $80,000 nearly one year after October 2025 crash CoinDesk
trechos: Crypto crumbles as anniversary of flash crash nears It was October 10, 2025, when bitcoin plunged from about $122,000 to $105,000, with much of the decline occurring within minutes.
- Bitcoin fell 4% to about a one-month low near $80,000, with the rest of the sector showing even steeper declines.

A modest early decline in bitcoin  on Thursday has accelerated, the price falling to about a one-month low just above $80,000 Bitcoin is down 4% over the past 24 hours, and is now lower by more than 8% since nearly hitting $87,000 just four days ago.
That’s masking far uglier action in the rest of the sector, with ether and XRP lower by about 6% over the past day and solana off 9%.
The fast selling comes as the one-year anniversary of the October 10, 2025, flash crash nears.

In a State Street survey of 300 asset managers, asset owners and wealth managers, published Tuesday, about 51% of respondents expect digital assets to become mainstream within the next five years, up from just 11% in 2024.

The survey also found that institutions hold an average of 11% of their portfolio in digital assets and expect that share to rise over the next three years, pointing to growing adoption even as prices fail to break out on the upside.

itens.titulo: On Establishes Google Cloud as Enterprise AI Backbone, Beginning with Agent-Led Cloud Migration
itens.descricao: On Establishes Google Cloud as Enterprise AI Backbone, Beginning with Agent-Led Cloud Migration PR Newswire
itens.texto:
Premium sportswear brand uses a multi-agent AI architecture to migrate 24 critical services to Google Cloud in weeks, establishing the foundation to modernize data platforms and deploy Gemini
ZURICH and SUNNYVALE, Calif., Oct. 8, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Google Cloud and premium sportswear brand On today announced that On used AI agents to migrate 24 core services to Google Cloud, cutting migration time from three months to just two weeks per service. A small team of On's internal engineers ran 15 migrations completely in-house through the new agent-led approach with under five minutes of planned downtime per service. Consolidating data, compute, and AI on Google Cloud has enabled On to scale workforce productivity and build custom internal agents using Gemini Enterprise.
As On scaled globally, the challenge was no longer simply running infrastructure efficiently, but creating a technology foundation capable of supporting the next phase of its growth. That meant reducing fragmentation between compute, data and AI, simplifying the architecture, and creating a common platform from which teams could build and deploy intelligent workflows and agents. On selected Google Cloud as that foundation.
"AI changes the economics of execution. We're seeing that firsthand when our engineers used AI agents to deliver a major cloud migration with no additional resources and zero business disruption," said Narek Verdian, chief technology officer, On. "The real opportunity is rethinking how technology work gets done, while ensuring human engineers remain accountable for the decisions that matter."
On's engineers saw productivity gains right away. Rather than relying on external systems integrators, internal engineers used agentic workflows to map complex, inconsistent deployment patterns across more than 20 code repositories in hours instead of days. By offloading mechanical tasks such as configuration scripting, data replication, and environment validation to AI agents, On protected its product engineering roadmap, eliminated the need for outside implementation support, and limited planned production cutover downtime to under five minutes per service.
"True agentic transformation requires a unified data and compute foundation," said Karthik Narain, chief product and business officer, Google Cloud. "On proved that specialized AI agents can fundamentally shift the efficiency and velocity of complex cloud migrations, setting the stage to modernize their critical data platforms on Google Cloud. Now, with Google Cloud serving as their enterprise AI backbone, On is using Gemini Enterprise to build and deploy custom agents that drive real business impact across their workforce."
Modernizing infrastructure through agentic AI
As On expanded globally, the premium performance brand faced a major engineering challenge: modernizing and migrating complex, deeply integrated microservices to Google Cloud without disrupting retail operations or slowing development.
To address this challenge, On's technology team and Google Cloud deployed a new paradigm for executing technical work using AI agents. Moving beyond standard developer assistance tools, toward coordinated, domain-specific AI agents capable of handling complex migration tasks end-to-end, On was able to work from one single agentic platform, leveraging secure and powerful models.
Bounded execution and human oversight
The multi-agent system divided the migration into specialized, automated steps, including codebase analysis, infrastructure configuration generation, translation pipeline creation, and testing validation. Engineers reviewed generated code, ran infrastructure changes, and authorized production cutovers. Agents were given defined tasks with clear checks, while consequential changes remained subject to human approval.
By shifting execution speed and capability to agentic AI, On unlocked substantial resource efficiency. For example, an external vendor initially submitted a $500,000 quote to migrate just a fraction of the microservices using traditional manual methods, On's internal engineering team was able to complete the broader project far faster without needing outside implementation resources.
The success of this migration showcases that in the era of agentic AI, constraints have shifted and the economics of this change pays off. This opens up the possibility to execute other complex workflows following a reusable blueprint, rethinking the work from the ground up, instead of automating a process that already exists.
On's AI ambitions go beyond its technology platform. The company rolled out Gemini Enterprise to every employee, empowering teams to build custom, no-code agents for executive reporting, market research, scheduling, onboarding, and more. It has also been a strategic partner to Google Cloud, providing feedback as a trusted tester of the new Gemini agent, Google Cloud's single universal agent for work.
About On
On was born in the Swiss Alps in 2010 with the mission to ignite the human spirit through movement – a mission that still guides the brand today. Sixteen years after market launch, On delivers industry-disrupting innovation in premium footwear, apparel and accessories for high-performance running, outdoor, training, all-day activities and tennis. On's award-winning CloudTec® and LightSpray™ innovation, purposeful design and groundbreaking strides within the circular economy have attracted a fast-growing global fan base – inspiring humans to explore, discover and Dream On.
On is present in more than 80 countries globally and engages with a digital community on www.on.com.
About Google Cloud
Google Cloud offers a powerful, optimized AI stack—including AI infrastructure, leading models like Gemini, data management capabilities, multicloud security solutions, developer tools and platform, as well as agents and applications—that enables organizations to transform their business for the Agentic Era.
